feedback.problem:
Which of the following functions satisfies the conditions of the mean value theorem over the interval $[-1,1]?$

- $f(x)=2|x|$
- $g(x)=|x-1|$
- $h(x)=|x+1|$
feedback.worked_solution:
For a function to satisfy the conditions of the mean value theorem over the interval $[-1,1],$ the function must be continuous on $[-1,1]$ and differentiable on $(-1,1).$

Let's check each function individually.

- The function $f(x)=2|x|$ is continuous on $[-1,1],$ but it has a corner in $x=0.$ Hence, it is not differentiable at $x=0,$ which means it is not differentiable on $(-1,1).$ Therefore, $f(x)$ does not satisfy the conditions of the mean value theorem.

- The function $g(x)=|x-1|$ is continuous on $[-1,1]$ and differentiable on $(-1,1)$ because it is equivalent to $p(x)=1-x$ over the given interval. Therefore, $g(x)$ satisfies the conditions of the mean value theorem. Note that the graph of $y=g(x)$ has a corner point at $x=1$ but this point does not lie inside $(-1,1).$

- The function $h(x)=|x+1|$ is continuous on $[-1,1]$ and differentiable on $(-1,1)$ because it is equivalent to $p(x)=x+1$ over the given interval. Therefore, $h(x)$ satisfies the conditions of the mean value theorem. Note that the graph of $y=h(x)$ has a corner point at $x=-1$ but this point does not lie inside $(-1,1).$

Therefore, only functions II and III satisfy the conditions for the mean value theorem over the interval $[-1,1].$
